{"level": 3, "why": "HOW I AM READING THE SCALE. [INFERENCE, from the enum alone] The tool gave me five numbered levels with no written text attached, so I am stating the criteria I believe I am selecting against: 0 = insufficient evidence to judge; 1 = fragile; 2 = adequate but with a live near-term funding or covenant issue; 3 = strong — survives the worst downturn visible in the bundle without external equity, with a named unverified item; 4 = unimpeachable, i.e. net cash and/or quantified covenant headroom. If the rubric's level-3 text in fact requires *disclosed* covenant headroom, that requirement is not met and the correct answer becomes level 0; the reader should overrule me on that basis if so.

1. LEVERAGE, GROSS AND NET.
[FACT] Total debt carrying value: "As of May 29, 2025, we had debt with a carrying value of $15.54 billion and may incur additional debt, including under our $3.50 billion Revolving Credit Facility." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:RiskFactors-DebtObligations)
[FACT] Balance sheet split: "Current debt | 538 | 431" and "Long-term debt | 15,003 | 12,966". (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:BS-Liabilities)
[FACT] "Cash and marketable investments totaled $12.21 billion as of May 29, 2025, and $9.15 billion as of August 29, 2024." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:MDA-Liquidity)
[FACT] "Total equity | 50,748 | 45,131" against "Total assets | $78,397 | $69,416". (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:BS-Equity)
[FACT] Of the $15.54bn, the note/term-loan component is "$12,434" and the balance is "Finance lease obligations | N/A | 5.30% | 538 | 2,569 | 3,107". (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-Table)
[INFERENCE, from 1–4] Gross debt of $15.54bn sits against $12.21bn of cash and marketable investments and $50.7bn of book equity, so the company is not in a net cash position but debt is a minority of the capital structure at book.
[DATA GAP] INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE — needed: a pre-computed net debt figure, net-debt/EBITDA, debt/equity and gross-leverage ratios, and peer-aligned leverage for Samsung/SK hynix/Kioxia/Sandisk. why: the bundle contains no <computed_metrics> section at all; it names competitors ("Kioxia Holdings Corporation; Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.; SK hynix Inc.; Sandisk Corporation; Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., Ltd. ('YMTC'); and ChangXin Memory Technologies, Inc. ('CXMT')") with no financial figures for any of them. would_change: if a computed net-leverage figure showed below ~1x trough EBITDA, level 4 becomes arguable; if it showed above ~3x, level 2.

2. THE MATURITY LADDER AND ITS COUPONS.
[FACT] "As of May 29, 2025, maturities of notes payable and the term loan by fiscal year were as follows: Remainder of 2025 | $— / 2026 | — / 2027 | — / 2028 | 600 / 2029 | 2,384 / 2030 and thereafter | 9,500". (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-Maturities)
[FACT] Finance-lease maturities are front-loaded by comparison: "Remainder of 2025 | $150 | $23 / 2026 | 674 | 91 / 2027 | 652 | 94 / 2028 | 630 | 87 / 2029 | 536 | 82 / 2030 and thereafter | 955 | 433 / Less imputed interest (490) | (138) / $3,107 | $672". (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Leases-Maturities)
[FACT] The 2025 issuances and their coupons: "On January 16, 2025, we issued $1.00 billion in aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured 2035 A Notes in a public offering. The 2035 A Notes bear interest at a rate of 5.80% per year and will mature on January 15, 2035." and "The 2032 Notes bear interest at a rate of 5.65% per year and will mature on November 1, 2032. The 2035 B Notes bear interest at a rate of 6.05% per year and will mature on November 1, 2035." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-SeniorUnsecuredNotes)
[FACT] The term loan is floating: "Borrowings under the Term Loan Agreement will generally bear interest at adjusted term SOFR plus an applicable interest rate margin ranging from 0.875% to 1.50%, depending on our corporate credit ratings." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-TermLoan)
[FACT] During the nine months the company retired its nearest maturities: prepayments of "2026 Term Loan A January 17, 2025 (897)", "2027 Term Loan A January 17, 2025 (1,037)", "2026 Notes | February 12, 2025 (500)", "2027 Notes May 27, 2025 (900)". (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-Activity)
[INFERENCE, from 8, 10, 11] There is no bond or term-loan wall inside three fiscal years — the first scheduled note/term-loan maturity is $600m in FY2028 — because the FY2026 and FY2027 maturities were prepaid during the period and replaced with 2032/2035 paper at 5.65%–6.05% and a 2029 floating-rate term loan.
[INFERENCE, from 9] The nearest-dated hard cash calls on debt are finance-lease payments of $674m in FY2026 and $652m in FY2027 (amounts shown before the $490m imputed-interest deduction), not refinancing risk.
[FACT] The debt trades below carrying value: "Notes payable and term loans | $12,183 | $12,434". (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-FairValue)

3. COVENANTS — THE OPEN ITEM.
[FACT] "The Term Loan Agreement requires us to maintain, on a consolidated basis, a net leverage ratio of total net indebtedness to adjusted EBITDA, as defined in the Term Loan Agreement and calculated as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, not to exceed 3.25 to 1.00, subject to a temporary four fiscal quarter increase in such maximum ratio to 3.75 to 1.00 following certain material acquisitions." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-TermLoan)
[FACT] "The Revolving Credit Facility contains the same net leverage ratio and substantially the same other covenants as the Term Loan Agreement." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-Revolver)
[FACT] Both are unsecured: "Our obligations under the Term Loan Agreement are unsecured." and "we terminated our existing undrawn credit facility and entered into a new five-year unsecured Revolving Credit Facility." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-TermLoan; MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-Revolver)
[DATA GAP] INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE — needed: the tested net-indebtedness-to-adjusted-EBITDA ratio as calculated at May 29, 2025, or the adjusted EBITDA figure as defined in the agreement. why: the bundle states the 3.25:1.00 threshold and states nothing about compliance or headroom; it contains no EBITDA line anywhere, and I am barred from deriving one. would_change: if headroom were disclosed as wide at trough earnings, level 4 becomes arguable; if the ratio were disclosed close to 3.25x, level 2.
[INFERENCE, from 14–16] This covenant is the single mechanism in the bundle that could convert a memory downturn into a forced financing event, because adjusted EBITDA is the denominator and DRAM/NAND pricing is the volatile input; that it is undisclosed is a finding against level 4, not a pass.

4. LIQUIDITY.
[FACT] "Cash and cash equivalents $10,163 | $7,041" and "Short-term investments | 648 | 1,065" and "Long-term marketable investments | 1,402 | 1,046". (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:BS-Assets)
[FACT] "As of May 29, 2025, $3.50 billion was available to draw under our Revolving Credit Facility." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:MDA-Liquidity)
[FACT] "Any amounts outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility would mature on March 12, 2030 and amounts borrowed may be prepaid without penalty." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Debt-Revolver)
[FACT] Management's own statement: "We expect that our cash and investments, cash flows from operations, funding from government incentives, and available financing will be sufficient to meet our requirements at least through the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:MDA-Liquidity)
[FACT] "As of May 29, 2025, $4.80 billion of our cash and marketable investments was held by our foreign subsidiaries." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:MDA-Liquidity)
[INFERENCE, from 18–20] Undrawn liquidity ($3.50bn revolver, five years to its own expiry) sits alongside $12.21bn of cash and investments and no note/term-loan maturity before FY2028, so near-term liquidity does not depend on capital-markets access.
[FACT] A qualifier on the revolver: "events and circumstances may occur which would cause us to not be able to satisfy applicable draw-down conditions and utilize our Revolving Credit Facility." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:RiskFactors-CashFlows)

5. ★ THE DOWNSIDE ARITHMETIC — WHAT THE BUNDLE ACTUALLY TESTS.
[FACT] The worst earnings period visible in the bundle is the first nine months of FY2024: "Operating income (loss) | 2,169 | 719 | 6,116 | (218)" and "Net income (loss) | $1,885 | $332 | $5,338 | $(109)", with a single quarter loss of "(1,234)" in Q1 FY2024. (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:IS-Consolidated; MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Equity-FY24)
[FACT] Gross margin in that stretch was "Gross margin | 3,508 | 38% | 2,963 | 37% | 1,832 | 27% | 9,819 | 38% | 2,876 | 17%" — 17% for 9M FY2024. (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:MDA-ConsolidatedResults)
[FACT] In that same loss-making stretch, "Net cash provided by operating activities | 11,795 | 5,102" — $5.10bn generated in 9M FY2024. (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:CF-Statement)
[FACT] Interest expense in that stretch: "Interest expense | (123) | (150) | (353) | (426)" — $426m for 9M FY2024. (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:IS-Consolidated)
[INFERENCE, from 24–27] At the worst earnings level the bundle contains — an operating loss and 17% gross margin — operating cash flow of $5,102m exceeded interest expense of $426m by an order of magnitude, so debt service was not at issue in that downturn.
[FACT] How that downturn was funded: "For the first nine months of 2024, net cash used for financing activities consisted primarily of $1.82 billion of repayments of debt... $384 million for payments of dividends to shareholders... partially offset by approximately $1.00 billion of proceeds from the issuance of the 2031 Notes." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:MDA-CashFlows)
[INFERENCE, from 29] In the bundle's one observed downturn the company net-repaid debt, kept paying the dividend, and raised no common equity for cash — direct evidence on the question asked.
[FACT] The capex offset: "We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion," and in 9M FY2024 "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment | (10,199) | (5,266)" — $5,266m. (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:MDA-Liquidity; MU-10Q-Q3FY25:CF-Statement)
[INFERENCE, from 26, 31] In 9M FY2024 capex of $5,266m modestly exceeded operating cash flow of $5,102m; at the ~$14bn annual capex run-rate now guided, a repeat of FY2024-level cash generation would leave capex substantially uncovered by operations, and the gap would have to come from the $12.21bn cash pile, the $3.50bn revolver, government incentives, or a capex cut — the risk factors state the company treats capex as discretionary ("we will need to add new DRAM wafer capacity... We retain discretion with respect to capacity and production volume ramp of each project").
[DATA GAP] INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE — needed: FY2023 full-year financials, the deepest trough the company references. why: the bundle mentions only its consequences ("in 2023, we recorded aggregate charges of $1.83 billion to write down the carrying value of our inventories to their estimated net realizable value") and a 2023 buyback figure, not the income statement, cash flow or debt balances of that year. would_change: if FY2023 showed negative operating cash flow with the current $15.54bn debt load, level 2; if it showed positive operating cash flow through the trough, level 4 becomes arguable.
[FACT] The scale of the cycle being insured against: "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range. In the past five years, annual percentage changes in NAND average selling prices have ranged from plus low-30% to a minus low-50% range." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:RiskFactors-ASP)

6. OFF-BALANCE-SHEET AND CONTINGENT ITEMS.
[FACT] Unconsolidated lease SPEs: "As of May 29, 2025, we had approximately $1.61 billion of finance lease liabilities and right-of-use assets under these arrangements." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-VIE)
[FACT] Executed but not commenced: "As of May 29, 2025, excluded obligations consisted of $1.02 billion of finance lease obligations over a weighted-average period of 14 years for gas supply arrangements deemed to contain embedded leases and equipment leases." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Leases)
[FACT] "As of May 29, 2025, we had purchase obligations of approximately $1.69 billion for the acquisition of property, plant, and equipment, substantially all of which is expected to be paid within one year." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:MDA-Liquidity)
[FACT] Litigation quantum: a jury "found that Micron should pay $425 million for infringement of the ‘912 patent and $20 million for infringement of the ‘417 patent," with USPTO decisions finding both patents' asserted claims unpatentable and appeals pending. (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Contingencies-Netlist)
[FACT] No accrual is disclosed: "We are unable to predict the outcome of any of the matters noted above and cannot make a reasonable estimate of the potential loss or range of possible losses." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Contingencies-Assessment)
[DATA GAP] INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE — needed: a litigation accrual balance (E-11) and a pension funded status. why: the bundle explicitly declines to estimate loss on the litigation, and on pensions contains only an AOCI component ("Pension liability adjustments | ... | 39 | ... | 38") with no obligation or asset figures. would_change: if a disclosed accrual or adverse final judgment materially exceeded $445m, the contingent claim would move from a rounding item against $12.21bn of liquidity toward a real one; a materially underfunded pension would do the same.
[FACT] A constraint that cuts both ways: CHIPS Act funds carry "clawbacks related to the failure to complete a project by an agreed upon completion date," and "There are restrictions on our payment of special and one-time dividends during the five-year period following the Idaho and New York award date of December 9, 2024. Share repurchases are permitted during the first two years of such five-year period up to amounts specified in the funding agreements." (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-CHIPS)
[INFERENCE, from 39] The CHIPS agreements restrain cash returns rather than requiring cash outflows, which is directionally protective of the balance sheet, but introduce a clawback contingency of undisclosed size.

7. DILUTION, THE ACTUAL QUESTION.
[FACT] "No shares were repurchased in the first nine months of 2025." and share count moved "1,263 shares issued and 1,119 outstanding (1,253 shares issued and 1,109 outstanding as of August 29, 2024)". (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Note-Equity; MU-10Q-Q3FY25:BS-Equity)
[FACT] The only equity inflows in the period were from compensation plans: "Stock issued under equity compensation plans 7 | 1 | 1 | — | — | — | 2" (Q1), "4 | — | 150 | — | — | — | 150" (Q2), "2 | — | 1 | — | — | — | 1" (Q3). (evidence_id: MU-10Q-Q3FY25:Equity-FY25)
[INFERENCE, from 41–42] Share count is creeping upward from equity compensation, not from capital raising; the bundle shows no equity issuance for cash in either the current period or the FY2024 downturn.

8. WHY 3 AND NOT 4 OR 2.
[INFERENCE, from 5, 12, 21, 28, 30, 43] Level 3 rather than 2: no note or term-loan maturity before FY2028, $12.21bn of cash and investments plus an undrawn $3.50bn revolver expiring 2030, unsecured debt, and a directly observed downturn (9M FY2024, 17% gross margin, operating loss) in which the company covered interest ten times over from operating cash flow, net-repaid debt, and issued no equity.
[INFERENCE, from 16, 33, 38] Level 3 rather than 4: the one covenant that matters is a 3.25:1.00 net-leverage test whose headroom the bundle does not disclose and whose denominator I cannot compute; the deepest trough in company history (FY2023) is not in the bundle; there is no peer-aligned leverage comparison; and gross debt exceeds cash and investments, so this is not a net-cash balance sheet.
[ASSUMPTION] I am assuming the ~$14bn 2025 capex guidance is management-discretionary in a downturn rather than contractually fixed; the bundle supports discretion over new fab ramps but quantifies only $1.69bn of firm PP&E purchase obligations, and I have not verified that the remainder could be deferred without penalty.", "what_would_move_it_down": "Disclosure of the tested net-indebtedness-to-adjusted-EBITDA ratio showing it sitting close to the 3.25-to-1.00 covenant ceiling at trough earnings would move this down one level, because the entire distinction I am drawing between "survives the cycle on its own cash" and "depends on lender forbearance" rests on headroom the bundle never quantifies."}
